questions.q: Who is a 'consumer' in the context of Home Economics and market trade?
options: An individual who buys raw materials to manufacture goods
An agency that regulates the prices of commodities
An individual who purchases and uses goods and services to satisfy personal or family needs
The seller who supplies goods directly from the factory
questions.explain: A consumer is the ultimate end-user who buys and uses products, goods, or services to fulfill personal or family desires and needs.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: The right of a consumer to be protected against goods and services that are hazardous to life and health is known as the right to:
options: Safety
Choose
Be heard
Consumer education
questions.explain: The Right to Safety guarantees that products available in the market should not cause harm or danger to the health and life of the consumer when used properly.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: The 'right to be informed' implies that consumers should:
options: Be forced to purchase products regardless of their contents
Be given full, truthful, and accurate facts about a product to make wise choices
Receive free samples of all newly manufactured products
Ignore the expiring dates written on the packaging
questions.explain: The Right to be Informed means consumers must be provided with complete and honest information regarding a product's quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard, and price.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: If a consumer buys a spoilt canned food, returns it to the seller, and requests a refund, which right are they exercising?
options: Right to seek redress
Right to a healthy environment
Right to be heard
Right to basic needs
questions.explain: The Right to Seek Redress empowers consumers to receive fair settlement or compensation (such as a refund or replacement) for just claims, including shoddy goods or unsatisfactory services.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: One of the major challenges consumers face in the modern market is the prevalence of:
options: Excessively cheap, high-quality original goods
Fake, substandard, and adulterated products
Too many strictly regulated truthful advertisements
Sellers offering free items daily
questions.explain: A major challenge for consumers is identifying and avoiding fake, substandard, or adulterated products which flood the market and can be harmful.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Why is 'misleading advertisement' considered a challenge for consumers?
options: It gives consumers entirely true information about product defects.
It forces sellers to reduce the price of the products below cost.
It deceives the consumer into buying products that do not perform as promised.
It increases the consumer's right to choose freely.
questions.explain: Misleading advertising manipulates or deceives consumers with false claims, leading them to spend money on goods or services that fail to deliver on expectations.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: When sellers hoard goods to make them scarce in the market, what is the usual effect on the consumer?
options: It makes the goods safer for immediate consumption.
It causes artificial scarcity, leading to unreasonable price hikes.
It forces the government to distribute free food items.
It improves the overall quality of the goods significantly.
questions.explain: Hoarding is a challenge because it restricts supply, creating an artificial scarcity that vendors use as an excuse to unfairly increase prices.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: In Nigeria, which of these is an example of a government body established to protect consumer rights?
options: Consumer Protection Council (CPC)
West African Examination Council (WAEC)
Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)
Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)
questions.explain: The Consumer Protection Council (CPC), now operating as FCCPC, is the primary regulatory body dedicated to protecting the rights and interests of consumers in Nigeria.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: What is the most appropriate first step a consumer should take when seeking redress for a defective product purchased from a store?
options: File a lawsuit in the Supreme Court immediately.
Arrest the seller with the help of local law enforcement.
Return the defective item to the retailer with the original purchase receipt.
Throw the item away and violently confront the shop owner.
questions.explain: The appropriate and legal first step for redress is to formally inform the retailer of the issue by returning the item along with proof of purchase (the receipt) for a replacement or refund.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: Why is keeping a receipt highly important in the procedure for seeking redress?
options: It acts as concrete evidence showing what was bought, when, where, and the exact price paid.
It allows the consumer to bypass paying taxes on future purchases.
It guarantees that the product will never spoil or get damaged.
It provides the personal home address of the manufacturer.
questions.explain: A receipt is vital documentary evidence required to process a refund or exchange, as it proves that the transaction actually occurred at that specific store.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: The term 'Redress' as an option for consumers basically means:
options: Changing one's clothing repeatedly before going to the market.
Repackaging an old product to look like it is new.
Receiving a remedy or compensation for a wrong, poor service, or defective product.
Forcing the consumer to pay twice for the same service.
questions.explain: In consumer rights, redress means to set right a wrong; it involves obtaining fair compensation or a remedy when a purchased product fails to meet the expected standards.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles
questions.subject: Pre Vocational Studies

questions.q: If a retailer adamantly refuses to replace a verified defective product, what is the next legal procedure for the consumer?
options: Destroy other items in the store equal to the value of the lost money.
Lodge a formal complaint in writing to a consumer protection agency.
Quietly accept the loss and never shop again.
Steal an alternative product when the retailer is not looking.
questions.explain: If direct negotiation with the seller fails, the proper procedure is to escalate the issue by reporting formally to relevant regulatory bodies like the CPC or NAFDAC for intervention.
